US standards lab says SMS is no good for authentication • The Register

This has been an automated message.
SMS is shit, voice is shit, and email is shit for verification purposes. Does that really surprise anyone? Proprietary apps might be better, but unless you build from source only marginally so.

Non-hardened communications can be intercepted by state-level actors. It's crazy not to assume so from the beginning.

This is probably a good time to point out that absolute data security against an attacker with unlimited resources is just flat-out impossible. What you need to do is assess the value of your communication (or other data) to a possible attacker, and make it expensive enough to obtain that data that it no longer makes economic sense for the attacker to bother.

So if you're just a pleb trying to access your personal bank account, SMS-based two-factor authentication is probably actually still fine. If you're in charge of personal security for a South American billionaire, you might want something a little more bulletproof.
